podcast-tuckercarlson-M5kcYlyyMcc:
Tucker Carlson devotes this episode to Christians in the Holy Land. He argues that Israel is purging them from the land where their faith began. He also argues that a plot of silence keeps Americans from noticing. His case draws on the decline of Christian communities in Israel and the Palestinian territories and on the pressures those communities describe.

Carlson frames the story as a betrayal hiding in plain sight: American Christians fund and defend a state he says mistreats their own brothers and sisters in the faith. Local Christians' accounts vary, and Israeli officials reject the charge entirely. The episode is preserved as Carlson's argument, which matters because it marks how far his break with pro-Israel conservatism has gone. Listeners can weigh his evidence against the denials and the history both sides cite.
the-history-of-england-in-three-volumes-: The History of England, Volume III, is credited on its title page to David Hume, Esq., printed in London in 1860. A second title page in the pages present assigns Volume III, from the accession of George III to the twenty-third year of the reign of Queen Victoria, to E. Farr and E. H. Nolan. A frontispiece of Queen Victoria is listed, and chapter one is headed George III, 1760-1765. Only the title pages and that chapter heading are present here.
the-life-of-hugo-grotius-with-brief-minu:
Charles Butler published his life of Hugo Grotius with John Murray in London in 1826, adding brief minutes of Dutch civil, church, and literary history. Opening pages name his chief sources. A French life by M. de Burigni, Englished in 1754, stands first among them.

Butler also used a two volume Latin defense of Grotius memory from 1727 and the Grotius article in Bayle dictionary. His dedication praises Grotius as a defender of civil and religious liberty. Readers get a jurist life set inside the wars, church fights, and learning of the Netherlands.
